signature.name: Kyiv Pechersk Lavra
signature.detail: A vast cave monastery and UNESCO World Heritage site, the spiritual heart of Kyiv and the reason many visitors come. Go early in the morning to avoid crowds, and dress modestly since it is an active monastery.

signature.name: St. Sophia's Cathedral
signature.detail: An 11th-century cathedral with stunning mosaics and frescoes, also a UNESCO site. Buy tickets at the bell tower entrance and allow an hour or two to explore the grounds.

signature.name: Maidan Nezalezhnosti
signature.detail: The central square of Kyiv and the stage for the country's modern history. It is free and open at all hours; visit in the evening when the fountains and lights are on.

signature.name: Andriyivskyy Descent
signature.detail: A cobbled historic street lined with art stalls, cafes and old houses, connecting the upper town to Podil. Walk it downhill in the late afternoon for the best light and atmosphere.

signature.name: St. Andrew's Church
signature.detail: A baroque church perched dramatically on a hill above Andriyivskyy Descent. Check opening hours before climbing up, as access is limited outside services.

signature.name: Golden Gate, Zoloti Vorota
signature.detail: The reconstructed main gate of the ancient Kyivan Rus city walls, right in the center. It is a quick stop near the metro of the same name and pairs well with a walk along the old fortifications.

signature.name: Motherland Monument, Kyiv
signature.detail: A colossal steel statue overlooking the Dnieper, one of the tallest in Europe. Combine it with a visit to the surrounding park and museum complex; the views over the river are the highlight.

food: Casual meal $6-12; mid-range dinner for two $25-45
stay: Good 3-4* hotel $50-90 a night; boutique stays $100-150
transport: Metro about $0.30 a ride; city taxis and ride-hailing are cheap
